By Helene DurandOctober 31, 2026 at 2:11 PM UTCBookmark

Vladimir Putin’s possible attendance at the Group of 20 leaders’ summit in Florida in December would risk regularizing Russia’s return to international forums while its war in Ukraine continues, according to the European Union’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas.
The US invitation to the Russian leader “poses a lot of big questions,” Kallas said on Saturday in an interview with Bloomberg Television. It risks “normalizing the war crimes being committed every day now” in Ukraine, she added.

item.title: Stadiums Rethink the Women’s Restroom
item.description:
Bloomberg This Weekend • Oct 31st, 2026
Stadiums Rethink the Women’s Restroom
On Bloomberg This Weekend, Writer and Journalist Benton Graham explains how stadiums and arenas are redesigning restrooms as women’s sports grow and venues recognize that equal restroom space does not necessarily mean equal access. Speaking with host Lisa Mateo, Graham says newer venues are dedicating more restroom capacity to women, while upgrades at older stadiums can carry significant costs.

item.title: Haunted Attractions Help Revive Neighborhoods
item.description:
Oct 31st, 2026
Haunted Attractions Help Revive Neighborhoods
Journalist Elizabeth Yuko tells Bloomberg This Weekend how haunted attractions are drawing visitors and investment to struggling neighborhoods, including Baltimore’s Old Town and former industrial districts in Kansas City and Salt Lake City. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Yuko explains how haunted-house operators can become unlikely partners in urban revitalization by investing in infrastructure, attracting businesses and finding new uses for neglected properties.

item.title: EU Foreign Policy Chief Warns Against Normalizing Russia
item.description:
Oct 31st, 2026
EU Foreign Policy Chief Warns Against Normalizing Russia
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas tells Bloomberg This Weekend that Russia is escalating its war in Ukraine and is not serious about peace, criticizing Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov’s statements at the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in Atlanta and warning against normalizing Moscow on the international stage. Speaking with host David Gura, Kallas also calls for a diplomatic solution to tensions with Iran and discusses efforts to deepen the EU’s relationship with Canada through greater cooperation on trade, energy and defense.

Senegalese lawmakers have again rejected the government’s revised 2026 finance law, prolonging a standoff that threatens to delay approval of a crucial International Monetary Fund program.
The parliament’s Finance and Budgetary Control Committee remained divided after talks late Friday over the treatment of special funds and assistance for vulnerable households, according to lawmakers and a government official involved in the discussions.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
As lawyers for Mercuria Energy Group presented the commodity giant’s case against the Baltic Exchange this week, a group of smartly dressed Norwegian businessmen listened intently to the arguments from the back of a packed London courtroom.
The executives, representing Oslo-listed Hunter Group ASA, have around $100 million riding on the outcome. The company is in a dispute with Mercuria over a charter deal linked to the TD3C index — the global benchmark oil tanker rate that the trading house claims the Baltic Exchange should have suspended because of disruptions caused by the Iran war.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Wall Street expects Democrats to win at least one of the houses of Congress in the US midterm elections on Tuesday, setting the stage for a potentially volatile ride in the stock and bond markets with artificial intelligence oversight, defense spending and crypto legislation on the table.
A UBS basket of stocks tied to Republicans has plunged since hitting a peak in August, badly lagging the S&P 500 Index. One major area where this could show up is in the AI trade that has been driving the stock market for the past few years, as Democrats are expected to push for stricter regulation and oversight of the technology. Meanwhile, local governments are under pressure to block data centers from being built in their communities.

item.title: Angola Plans to Cut Fuel Subsidies Without Price Increases
item.description: Angola, sub-Saharan Africa’s second-largest oil producer, plans to cut spending on fuel subsidies in 2027 without significant increases in pump prices, relying instead on other measures to reduce costs.

item.title: Chocolate Price Spook Families for Halloween
item.description: Halloween candy is getting more expensive as higher labor, energy and transportation costs continue to pressure food prices. Stew Leonard Jr., CEO of Stew Leonard’s, says bags of popular candy are up about 50 cents from last year, prompting some shoppers to trade down to cheaper options. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss how affordability is changing consumer behavior, and how both environmental and economic changes are impacting the business. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto Hack Reignites Regulatory Debate
item.description: A $6 billion crypto hack is putting digital-asset security back in the spotlight. Former CFTC chairman J. Christopher Giancarlo, known as “CryptoDad”, argues the attack exposed vulnerabilities at an individual firm rather than a failure of underlying blockchain technology. He is also calling for the US to take a more aggressive approach to state-sponsored cyberattacks. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the fallout from the hack and why he believes prediction markets should be regulated federally by the CFTC rather than by individual states. (Source: Bloomberg)
